absent: Selection policy and priority index maintenance behind lowest processor choice and overload helpers.
Internals of balanced runqueue locking, task movement, rescheduling and pushable list management.
Root domain lifecycle, allocation, and deferred free routine beyond the put path.
Complete real time bandwidth timer, throttling, runtime enable and disable behavior.
Fair runqueue load weight, timeline, PELT and throttling clock mechanics.
Deadline bandwidth validation and topology rebuild effects.
Exact time conversions for round robin slice and watchdog bounds.

findings.text: Global interrupt work handler drains locally pushable real time work under runqueue protection then forwards the overload signal to another overloaded processor or releases the domain reference when none remains.
Global domain release decrements the reference count and only when reaching zero schedules deferred reclamation through read copy update.
Wakeup hook for real time class evaluates placement, reschedule need, migratability and donor priorities to decide whether to attempt pushing tasks elsewhere.
Processor online and offline hooks for real time class synchronize overload marking, runtime allowance and the shared priority index, using an invalid marker when going offline.

Class change hooks handle departure by pulling work when the last queued real time task leaves, and arrival by queuing pushes for migratable overloaded cases plus preemption when the newcomer outranks the donor.
Priority change hook for queued real time tasks requests a pull when a running donor loses priority and requests rescheduling when a higher priority runnable exists relative to donor or tracked best.

Periodic tick for real time class refreshes execution accounting and limit supervision, and for round robin policy manages slice countdown with reload and end of queue repositioning followed by rescheduling when needed. Interval query reports configured slice for round robin and zero otherwise.

Lowest queue search performs bounded retries for a distinct processor with strictly more favorable tracked priority, abandoning on equal or worse priority, affinity loss, migration disablement, or change of the pushable head, while holding balanced locks on success.

Single push is gated on overload indication and presence of a pushable head, avoids self migration, protects the candidate with a reference across potential lock release, relocates it on success with remote rescheduling, and revalidates or retries when state shifted during the search.

Push driver repeatedly attempts single pushes until stable. When the head cannot migrate, it optionally tries to offload the running real time donor through an asynchronous stop request instead of migrating the head.

Overload balancing forms a chain where each processor drains its own pushable work and then passes a single wakeup signal onward until no overloaded processor remains, at which point the domain reference is dropped.

Round robin slice cycles through countdown, reload to configured length on expiry, conditional requeue when the hierarchy is not solitary, and reschedule to effect rotation; first in first out policy bypasses this cycle.

Supervision has active and empty configurations. Active form samples soft and hard execution limits, counts at most one timeout per tick period, and notifies the timer subsystem when the count exceeds the derived bound; the alternate form performs no action.
Throttle query resolves either the per group per processor queue or the per processor queue depending on build configuration and reports its throttled condition.
A dedicated mutex serializes changes to real time bandwidth constraints and schedulability evaluation across groups.

Group schedulability proposal carries a target group with period and runtime. Validation rejects runtime above period unless infinite, rejects starvation of existing real time members when disabling, enforces the global ratio cap, and rejects children sums exceeding the parent allowance. Membership scan skips autogroups.

Global validation checks runtime against period and a hardware ceiling plus hierarchy consistency when enabled. Control handler serializes updates, rolls back period and runtime on failure, coordinates deadline bandwidth, and rebuilds topology. Round robin handler normalizes the slice control and restores default on nonpositive input.
Asymmetric capacity record chains through lists, supports deferred reclamation, stores a capacity value and a trailing flexible processor set.
Real time priority array combines a bitmap with delimiter and per level queue heads. Bandwidth control combines a nested runtime lock with period, runtime, timer and active indication.
Deadline bandwidth record combines a protection lock with current and total bandwidth accounting.

Fair bandwidth control has a full form with lock, period, quota, runtime, burst, hierarchical quota, idle and activity flags, timers, throttled list and statistics, and an empty form when the feature is disabled.

Task group anchors cgroup state, optional fair and real time hierarchies with shares and bandwidth, scheduler extension state, reclamation and linkage for parent and children, plus autogroup, fair bandwidth and clamp controls when enabled. Visitor is a callback returning status for a group and opaque data.
Balance callback chains through a next link and carries a function invoked with the runqueue.

Fair runqueue aggregates load and queue counts, vruntime and weight summaries, timeline and current pointers, load tracking, removal statistics under their own cache aligned lock, and for grouped builds hierarchy linkage, ownership, leaf tracking and throttling clocks and lists.
Queued state uses value one and migrating state uses value two.
Load average period uses value thirty two and load average maximum uses value forty seven thousand seven hundred forty two.

Nice zero load is a power of two derived from a shift that has single and double fixed point variants. Root group load aliases that value. Share floor is two and ceiling is two hundred sixty two thousand one hundred forty four.
Infinite runtime is all bits set in sixty four bits. Deadline scale uses value ten. Scheduler sugov flag uses bit twenty eight, and deadline flags combine reclaim plus overrun plus sugov.

Extension runqueue flags use bit zero for online, bit one for tick control, bit five for clock validity, bit six for pending balance callback, bits seven and eight for subordinate and root idle renotify, and bits sixteen and seventeen for wakeup and dispatch context.
Load decay table provides thirty two inverse coefficients for geometric weighting. Scheduler header defines an inclusion guard macro.

Bandwidth and removal locks nest inside runqueue protection. Lowest queue acquisition uses paired balanced locking of source and destination with full revalidation if the source lock was dropped. Overload forwarding lock protects selection of the next target.

Push path hazards include priority change, migration, affinity change and head replacement while locks are released, plus priority inversion between head and donor requiring rescheduling rather than migration. Domain teardown hazards require reference counting with deferred free to avoid use after release.
